newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's funds expect to collect 7 trillion pta in 1997. [CORRECTED 18:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Spain's funds expect to collect 7 trillion pta in 1997. [CORRECTED 18:02 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects from billions to trillions in headline and text throughout.)

Spanish investment and pension funds expect to collect around seven trillion pesetas of fresh money in 1997 which could create a speculative bubble if new investment opportunities fail to appear, Inverco said on Monday.

"It's a total of seven trillion pesetas, which is more than double the central government financing requirements," Marian Rabadan, chairman of the Spain's association of investment and pension funds (Inverco), told reporters.
"That leaves a lot of money, around four trillion pesetas, to finance the private sector of the economy," he said.
Rabadan urged private companies to list their shares or issue bills and bonds to absorb the new liquidity, saying there was currently little demand for the funds.
If no new borrowing requirements surface, there was a risk the money would be spent in secondary markets, falsely inflating their value.
"The risk is a speculative bubble," he said.

Rabadan said that so far this month new investments in funds had reached about one trillion pesetas and he forecast the capital of investment funds could hit 25 trillion pesetas by the end of the year from 18.7 trillion reached at the end of 1996.
"We hope to end this year with a total capital at 24 or more likely at 25 trillion pesetas," he said.
In addition, he said the industry hopes to collect an additional trillion each in pension and in insurance funds.
1996 was an exceptional year during which the capital of investment funds rose by 53.4 percent and the average yield was at 9.93 percent, three times the inflation rate of 3.2 percent.
During 1997, investment funds hope to offer a yield of around five percent.
"It'll be a little lower in the money market sector, a little higher in the bonds, and in between 10 to 15 percent in the equities' funds," he said.
